description: ATUS-Commuting constructs commuting measures from American Time Use Survey activity diaries. Gray Kimbrough supplies Stata scripts implementing a trip-tour method, with a master file that calls the preparation stages. Hierarchical ATUS-X extracts are converted into activity records linked to respondent and household characteristics. Geographic coverage is the United States, while the observation years and diary timing follow the extracts selected by the user. The output can help prepare travel-demand assumptions or calibrate commuting behaviour in related transport simulations. Code is free under Apache-2.0, but running it requires Stata and separately obtained survey inputs. A limitation is that the supplied sample-selection script applies age and weekday filters used in the paper; the README says these may be unsuitable for another analysis. Input paths and extraction scripts also need adaptation. No survey archive was downloaded and no individual travel records were inspected.
